_README: THIS FILE LEAVES THE ENGINE IN WAVE 9. It is installation DATA sitting in engine code:
which instances of each connection exist, what each instance's secret files are called on
the box, which capability needs which connection, and the consumers that have no grants to
derive their connections from. An integration manifest (integrations/<id>/integration.json)
describes the VENDOR and cannot carry any of this, because it is the same for every
installation and none of this is.
Lifted verbatim from packages/agent-kit/src/connections.ts as it stood at commit b4ff019.
Nothing was renamed and no value changed. The names inside it (org ids, agent instance ids,
secret file names, one base URL) belong to the one existing installation; wave 9 moves this
whole file out of the engine, which is why it is ONE file and not eight.
Edit this, or an integration manifest, then run:
pnpm -C packages/agent-kit run generate:connections
That ONE command writes BOTH generated files (LAR-76):
packages/agent-kit/src/connections.ts         — what the console shows
packages/agent-kit/src/integration-secrets.ts — what the keeper may MOUNT
`secretEnv` on an instance is what the second one is made of: secret file name -> the
environment variable the runtime reads that file's path from. A secret with no entry is a
credential the keeper will NOT mount from an agent definition. Declare `secretEnv` on an
instance and you must declare it for EVERY secret of that instance — half a credential pair
is worse than none. An env key may appear once across the whole file.
`note` is emitted as a comment above the rendered object; `instancesNote` above its
`instances:` line; `capabilityNotes[c].above` / `.inline` around a capability's line.

connections.label: Google (Gmail + Calendar)
instancesNote: One OAuth client per org. Internal consent only accepts users of that client's Workspace,
which is why a user in another Workspace cannot go through the heiberg client (ORB-28).

connections.label: LiteLLM gateway
note: No configEnv: GATEWAY_URL is read directly via ctx.env at each build site today, and adding
it here would change gen-compose output for no gain. Left deliberately.

connections.label: Karakeep (bookmarks)
note: LAR-76: added because the keeper already mounts this key from an agent definition and no
list said so. Read by the digest schedule alongside the KARAKEEP_URL environment binding.

connections.label: Signal spine (bearer token)
note: LAR-76: the bearer token for the installation's own signals endpoint (SIGNAL_SPINE_URL).
Already mountable by the keeper; declared here so it is visible and rotatable like the rest.

connections.label: Google Places (API key)
note: A plain API key, NOT the OAuth client above: different credential, different custody, and
the travel tools treat it as optional. LAR-76 closes the gap the secret lint reported —
this key was read in code and declared nowhere.

connections.label: AeroDataBox (flight status)
note: LAR-76: optional third-party flight-status key the keeper already mounts.

connections.label: Strava (OAuth client)
note: LAR-76: optional. The file names below are the ones the keeper mounts today; the adapter's
own hard-coded fallback path spells them with an agent prefix, which only ever applies when
the environment variables below are unset — the keeper always sets them.

identity.inline: reads the box's own user_aliases registry — no external credential

above: Fans out over capabilities Saga already holds — so it needs their credentials, and no new one.

obligation.inline: reads/writes the box's own obligation_threads table — no external credential

note: Reads Calendar through agent-runtime's resolver, Notion with its own token, and — since
ORB-39 Phase 4 — Twenty, for the People projection (read-only, keyed by email).
consumers.name: notion-sync
